title: Appendix C — Motives and Motifs in the Poetry of Marianne Moore
folder: Burke - Motives and Motifs in Marianne Moore
role: Third Appendix essay. Burke applies the dramatism apparatus across Marianne Moore's complete poetry (oeuvre-level rather than single-text analysis as in the Keats appendix). The essay tracks recurring motifs (animal-imagery, armor-and-fragility, the moral attention to attentiveness itself) and reads them as expressions of a stable underlying motive-structure: a particular configuration of act / scene / agent across Moore's body of work. The methodological move from single-text to author-oeuvre dramatism is the chapter's signature contribution. Phase 3 will use it as the template for the dissertation's empirical-adaptation chapter at oeuvre or community scale (analogous to a game-studio's body of work, or a player's body of play across games). Heavy verse-quotation produces lower character density per OCR'd page (Phase 0 sampled PDF p.515 yielded ~1531 chars vs. volume average ~2500) — Phase 2 must preserve poetry line-break structure.
